source_refs.note: Topic 12.8 with the For Your Information box (PDF 274, printed 271).

blocks.text: All nuclear processes, such as nuclear reactions and nuclear decays, obey conservation laws, such as:

items: Conservation of energy, momentum and charge. It includes the nucleon number and the charge number (Z).

blocks.caption: For Your Information: hadrons and non-hadrons
rows: protons, neutrons, omega, sigma and lambda particles

blocks.prompt: Nitrogen-14 (Z = 7) bombarded by an alpha particle gives oxygen-17 (Z = 8). What is the product particle, and show that the nucleon number and charge number are conserved (numerical 12.3, 12.4).
blocks.explanation: Nitrogen-14 + helium-4 -> oxygen-17 + X. Nucleons: 14 + 4 = 18 = 17 + A, so A = 1. Charge: 7 + 2 = 9 = 8 + Z, so Z = 1. The product is a proton (hydrogen-1). Both the nucleon number (18 before and after) and the charge number (9 before and after) are conserved.

items: Nuclear reactions and decays conserve energy, momentum and charge (including nucleon number and charge number Z), baryon number and lepton number. Hadrons: mesons (pions, kaons) and baryons (p, n, omega, sigma, lambda); non-hadrons: leptons, photons, gravitons.
